classification.difficultyReason: Directly apply the vertical line test and read graphical extents, distinguishing attained extrema from excluded asymptotic limits.

content.prompt: For each of the following graphs, state if it is a function, write down the domain and write down the range.

spec.description: Circle centred at the origin with radius 3, unfilled. Preserve four labelled extrema and positive axis arrows.
spec.answerVisibility: The entire supplied relation is visible in the question.

answer.worked: A vertical line through the interior of the circle meets it twice, so the relation is not a function. The leftmost and rightmost points have $x=-3$ and $x=3$, giving domain $[-3,3]$. The lowest and highest points have $y=-3$ and $y=3$, giving range $[-3,3]$. All four extrema are included.

spec.description: Upward parabola through the origin, vertex (1,-1), dashed coordinate guides and continuation arrows. Equation used only to construct the supplied graph.
spec.answerVisibility: Vertex guides and their source numerical labels remain visible.

answer.worked: Every vertical line meets the parabola once, so it is a function. The branches continue indefinitely to the left and right, giving domain $\mathbb{R}$. The minimum value is $-1$ at the vertex, and the graph extends upwards without bound, giving range $[-1,\infty)$.

spec.description: Unscaled right-opening parabola with vertex at the origin and arrows on both branches. No numerical ticks are supplied.
spec.mathematics: A representative parametrisation (t^2,t) preserves the unscaled source relation.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied relation and axes are shown.

answer.worked: For each $x>0$, a vertical line meets both branches, so the relation is not a function. The graph starts at $x=0$ and continues to the right, giving domain $[0,\infty)$. Its branches extend upwards and downwards without bound, giving range $\mathbb{R}$.

spec.description: Symmetric schematic curve attaining its minimum at the origin, with both tails approaching the dashed line y=1 from below. Bézier segments preserve the supplied qualitative graph without assigning a formula.
spec.mathematics: Domain R, minimum 0 attained, horizontal asymptote y=1 approached from below.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied asymptote label and minimum remain visible.

answer.worked: Each vertical line meets the curve once, so it is a function. The curve continues in both horizontal directions, giving domain $\mathbb{R}$. It attains $y=0$ at the origin and approaches $y=1$ from below without reaching it, giving range $[0,1)$.

spec.description: Circle centred at (1,2), radius 1, tangent to the y-axis. Dashed guides locate the centre and upper extent. The centre dot locates the centre and is not an isolated relation point.
spec.answerVisibility: Preserve the supplied centre marker and labels 1, 2 and 3.

answer.worked: A vertical line through the interior of the circle meets its circumference twice, so the relation is not a function. The centre is $(1,2)$ and the radius is $1$. Its horizontal extrema are $x=0$ and $x=2$, giving domain $[0,2]$. Its vertical extrema are $y=1$ and $y=3$, giving range $[1,3]$.

spec.description: Unscaled positive decreasing curve, continuing upwards to the left and approaching the x-axis from above to the right. Bézier segments preserve the qualitative source graph without assigning an equation or numerical intercept.
spec.mathematics: Domain R, positive unbounded range, horizontal asymptote y=0.
spec.answerVisibility: No numerical labels or equation are added.

answer.worked: Each vertical line meets the curve once, so it is a function. The graph continues in both horizontal directions, giving domain $\mathbb{R}$. It stays above the $x$-axis, approaches $y=0$ without reaching it and rises without bound to the left, giving range $(0,\infty)$.
